newsitem.title: INDIA: New crop arrivals soften India palm olein imports.
newsitem.headline: New crop arrivals soften India palm olein imports.

text.p: India's palm olein imports have softened with new oilseed crop arrivals despite a surge in demand ahead of the festival season, industry officials said on Wednesday.
"Palm olein imports have started tapering because the domestic crop has started arriving now," said an official with a leading industrial house.

"Domestic edible oil prices have fallen by nearly 30 rupees per 10 kgs in the past 20 days as new oilseeds have started arriving in the local markets," said Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd.

Traders said domestic groundnut oil was currently quoted at 4,150-4,200 per quintal, down from 4,470 rupees per quintal three weeks ago. Palm olein was quoted at around 2,650 per quintal, after being traded at around 2,950 per quintal 20 days ago.
"Prices are expected to soften further when the new crop starts arriving in full flow after the first half of November and the festival season is over," Shah said.
Demand for edible oil almost triples during the Hindu festival period from September to November when supplies are at their tightest.
"Palm olein imports are expected to be around 80,000 tonnes during October," Shah said.

Industry officials said palm olein imports in October were expected to be much lower than previous estimates of 150,000 tonnes due to adequate supplies and monsoon rains that would be good for new crops.
India imported nearly 650,000 tonnes of edible oil between June and August.
Shah said around 80,000 bags per day (one bag weighs 80 kgs) of the new groundnut crop had started arriving in western Indian markets.

He said winter groundnut production was expected to be around 5.35 million tonnes compared with 4.6 million last year due to good rains. Groundnut accounts for nearly 40 percent of the country's oilseed output.
"No new contracts for edible oil imports are taking place now for future imports as domestic supplies will start firming up from now," said an official with a leading oil importer.
Industry officials had earlier estimated India's edible oil imports in 1995/96 (November-October) at 1.25-1.3 million tonnes, nearly one million tonnes of it palm olein.
India imported about 700,000 tonnes of edible oil in 1994/95.
